name: World music
editorial_article: "World music" is a broad, often debated umbrella term used to categorize musical traditions, folk styles, and contemporary fusion genres that originate outside of the conventional Western pop, rock, and classical spheres. While its origins as a formal industry designation date back to the late 1980s—when British record labels sought a cohesive retail label for African, Latin American, and other international imports—the concept has roots in earlier attempts to describe "exotic" influences on Western music. The term serves as a testament to the increasing globalization of the recording industry and the multicultural shifts in Western societies during the late 20th century. \n\nMusically, the category is notoriously diverse, encompassing everything from traditional, instrument-heavy folk performances like klezmer, highlife, or Celtic music to "world beat" fusions that blend indigenous percussion and non-Western scales with danceable, modern production techniques. Because it functions largely as a catch-all retail category, it has faced sustained criticism for potentially marginalizing non-Western artists by grouping vastly different cultural expressions into a single, loosely defined "other." Despite these criticisms, the term remains a significant indicator of how global migration and digital accessibility have reshaped the listener's relationship with music. It has paved the way for cross-pollination in jazz, classical, and electronic spheres, fostering a greater appreciation for modal scales, polyrhythms, and vocal melismas that were once relegated to the fringes of the global North. Today, world music acts as both a commercial gateway and an educational tool, encouraging cross-cultural dialogue through the shared language of melody and rhythm.

citations.title: A Short History Of World Music - An Introduction To The Genre

editorial_definition: A broad, catch-all retail and marketing classification for music originating outside the traditional Western popular or classical mainstream, encompassing both authentic regional folk traditions and contemporary fusions.
